summary: Douglas J. Penick is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Princeton University from circa 1962 to 1966 and studied under the traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa in 1971.

Douglas L. Berger works in philosophy, Sinology, and Indology. He served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Southern Illinois University (attested 2007–2014) and later as Professor and Director of the Centre for Intercultural Philosophy at Leiden University (attested 2026).

Douglas Osto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a master's at the University of Washington (~1996–1998) and a PhD at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel (~2000–2004), becoming a Senior Lecturer at Massey University in 2005.

Douglas Q. Adams is a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Chicago from circa 1968 to 1972 and held a post at the University of Idaho from circa 1972 to 2010.
Dragana Majhen works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed a master's degree at the University of Manitoba under thesis advisor Albert Welter (attested 2010).

Dragomir Dimitrov works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA under Michael Hahn and a PhD at the University of Marburg (-2004), where he also held posts, later becoming a Foreign Adjunct Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University.
Drodul Dorji Tenzin studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Drodul Pawo Dorje studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Ayu Khandro, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Drolkar Chungchung studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Drolma is a Tibetologist who earned an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).
Drubwang Shakya Shri studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and he taught Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.
Drukpa Lama Rik Drol Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dudjom Rinpoche (1904–1987) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jampal Delek Nyima, Min Ling Orgyen Namdrol Gyatso, and Pé Kö Lama Könchok Rabten, and taught numerous disciples, including Keith Dowman and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1904–1987) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under multiple masters including Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo, founded the International Nyingma Society, and taught many students, including Matthew T. Kapstein, Alexander Berzin, and Sogyal Rinpoche.

Duncan Ryūken Williams specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. After earning his PhD at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, he held posts at UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.
Dung Ngoc Duong specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Boston University under the doctoral supervision of Malcolm David Eckel (attested 2001).

Dungkar Lobzang Trinle (1927–1997) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies educated at Sera and Gyuto Monasteries. He served as a professor at Minzu University of China and Tibet University, and directed the Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences.

Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was an Indologist educated at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta. He held professorships at Scottish Church College, Narasinha Dutt College, and Sanskrit College and University.
Durga Prasad Dikshit specializes in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under teachers R. K. Dikshit and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi, and completed his doctoral studies under Baij Nath Puri.
Dwijendra Narayan Jha (1940–2021) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at Patna University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta.
